reading: こんにちは
context: Standard daytime greeting (roughly 11:00–17:00). Use おはようございます in the morning, こんばんは in the evening.

jp: ありがとうございます
reading: ありがとうございます
context: Polite thank-you. ありがとう alone is casual (friends); どうも is a casual thanks with a slight bow.

reading: すみません
context: Triple-duty: 'excuse me' to get attention, light apology, or 'thank you' (e.g. to a clerk). ごめんなさい is a stronger apology (to a person you wronged).

reading: おねがいします
context: Universal polite request — 'please do this for me'. Pairs with ありがとうございます in service encounters.

reading: はじめまして
context: Said on first introduction. Followed by どうぞよろしくおねがいします ('please be kind to me').

reading: これをください
context: Point at the item. あれ (that one) for an item across the counter; それ (that one) for something near the listener. ください = please give me.

reading: おねがいします
context: Said when the clerk confirms your order. The 'seal' on a service transaction.

reading: いくらですか
context: The price question. 全部でいくらですか = 'how much in total?' (useful at the register).

reading: トイレはどこですか
context: The most-asked traveler question. お手洗い (otearai) is the formal word; トイレ is universally understood. 化粧室 (keshoushitsu) = powder room (often more polite in upscale hotels).

reading: おすすめ は なん ですか
context: Asking the staff. 人気 (ninki) = 'popular';  signature (kiseki) = 'house special'. Both pair with は何ですか.

reading: えき は どこ ですか
context: Replace 駅 with any landmark: コンビニ (konbini), ホテル (hoteru), 空港 (kuukou).

jp: 右に曲がってください
reading: みぎ に まがって ください
context: 左 = hidari (left). Go straight = まっすぐ (massugu). The te-form + ください gives polite instructions.

reading: ここで おります
context: Said to the driver/announce button. おります is the humble verb for 'to get off' (yourself). 降ります is the plain equivalent.

reading: あるいて いけま すか
context: Asking a destination's distance. 遠い (tooi) = far; 近い (chikai) = near. バスで行けますか = 'can I take a bus there?'

reading: でぐち は どこ ですか
context: Subway/station exit. 入口 (iriguchi) = entrance. 北口 (kitaguchi) = north exit; 中央口 (chuouguchi) = central gate.

reading: カード は つかえます か
context: Many small shops are cash-only. 現金 (genkin) = cash. 両替 (ryougae) = currency exchange.

reading: ふくろ を ください
context: Plastic bags cost ¥3–¥10 since the 2020 regulation. 大丈夫です ('daijoubu desu') = 'no, thanks' (to decline).

reading: おかいけい おねがいします
context: In a restaurant, ask for the bill. 割り勘 (warikan) = split the bill; 持ち帰り (mochikaeri) = takeout.

jp: 試着してもいいですか
reading: しちゃく しても いい ですか
romaji: shichaku shite mo ii desu ka
context: Clothing shops. 別のサイズ (betsu no saizu) = 'a different size'. あります = 'we have it'.

reading: めんぜい できま すか
context: Tourists with passport spending ≥¥5,000 (general goods) or ¥5,000 (consumables) at one shop. Show your passport at the register.
